processing_steps.method: standard induction melting in an alumina crucible
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Fe–Al base alloys were prepared by standard induction melting in an alumina crucible under inert gas.

processing_steps.method: drop casting into a 25 mm diameter cylindrical copper mould
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Drop casting into a 25 mm diameter cylindrical copper mould produced samples with grain size of the order of 0.25 mm.
Cooling after solidification was sufficiently slow to allow a high degree of B2 order for Al-rich alloys (the Fe–35% Al alloy) and a good degree of DO3 order for alloys containing 25–30% Al.

Compression samples were cut from the ingots by spark machining, either as 3 mm diameter or as 5 mm × 5 mm square cross-section samples, of height twice the diameter or width; flat surfaces polished on 1500 grade abrasive paper before testing.

Tested at room temperature to a strain of 2–3% at a nominal strain rate of 3×10⁻⁴ s⁻¹; compression axis parallel to the cylinder axis of the cast samples; smooth onset of plasticity with no discrete yield points and slightly curved stress–strain behaviour.

structures.overall_structure: After 2–3% room-temperature compression, the Fe–35% Al alloy (B2 ordered with some degree of DO3 order) deforms by B2 superdislocations composed of two (1/2)⟨111⟩ partials lying close together; the dislocation substructure consists of many straight, near-screw superdislocations together with edge dipole segments and loops, plus weak remnant (APBII) fringes from partial destruction of DO3 order.

microstructure_list.region: thin foils cut from the centre of the deformed samples, perpendicular to the stress axis

defects.type: B2 superdislocations consisting of two (1/2)⟨111⟩ partials lying close together
edge dipole segments (large number) and dipole loops
APBII remnant (weak) fringes from destruction of DO3 order

defect_interactions.interaction_type: dipole formation on moving screw superdislocations at obstacles
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Several dipole segments are pulled out of the moving screw superdislocations where these encounter some obstacle (Fig. 17, right); the resulting large number of dipole segments is clearly seen in the ±g pair of images (Fig. 18), where short dipole segments reverse contrast.

interfaces.slip_behavior: Deformation is carried by B2 superdislocations, each composed of two (1/2)⟨111⟩ partials; these partials lie close together (small separation, not widely dissociated) because of the higher APBI fault energy in this Al-rich alloy, and the dislocations are generally straight and mostly in near-screw orientations.
interfaces.phase_evolution: Movement of the paired-partial B2 superdislocations destroys some of the DO3 order in the Fe–35% Al alloy, leaving weak remnant (APBII) fringes (Fig. 19).
interfaces.interface_notes: In contrast to Fe–25% Al (loosely coupled partials due to low APB energies), the higher APBI fault energy of Fe–35% Al keeps the two (1/2)⟨111⟩ partials closely spaced.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: 3 mm diameter or 5 mm × 5 mm square cross-section, of height twice the diameter or width
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Compression axis parallel to the cylinder axis of the cast samples; tested to a strain of 2–3%; smooth onset of plasticity with no discrete yield points and slightly curved stress–strain behaviour.

yield_strength.direction: compression (parallel to the casting cylinder axis)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL 2010 microscope; dislocations imaged in Bright Field and Weak Beam modes, planar (shear or thermal) faults in various dark field modes
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Thin foils prepared from the centre of the deformed samples perpendicular to the stress axis; dislocation Burgers vectors identified by imaging with a variety of g vectors, generally in Bright Field mode (e.g. g = 1 1 0, 2 0 0; ±g pairs)
characterization_methods.purpose: Examine the dislocation structures produced by 2–3% room-temperature deformation of Fe–35% Al
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe–35% Al deforms by B2 superdislocations composed of two closely spaced (1/2)⟨111⟩ partials that are generally straight and near-screw oriented, with many edge dipole segments and loops; weak remnant (APBII) fringes indicate partial destruction of DO3 order.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: 25% nitric acid in methanol mixture, about 20 V, -30 °C
characterization_methods.purpose: Prepare thin foils for TEM from the deformed samples

unmapped_findings: Fe–35% Al (at.%) was one of the binary alloys prepared with Al contents of 15, 20, 25, 28, 30 and 35% Al by induction melting and drop casting (b0022).

The higher APBI fault energy of the Al-rich Fe–35% Al alloy keeps the two (1/2)⟨111⟩ partials of the B2 superdislocation closely spaced, in contrast to the loosely coupled partials in the lower-APB-energy Fe–25% Al alloy (b0046).
For Fe–35% Al, the movement of the paired-partial B2 superdislocations destroys some of the DO3 order, producing the weak remnant fringes seen in Fig. 19 (b0046).

Work hardening rate increases in the ordered state and shows a sharp maximum near 28% Al, falling to a moderate value (~5–6 GPa over 35–40% Al); the addition of about 0.1% B caused little consistent change in work hardening rate (b0012, b0029, figure_002).

APB energies used to interpret the Fe–35% Al structures: the APBI energy in B2 order rises strongly with Al content (up to ~120 mJ/m² near 36% Al), while the DO3 APBI and APBII energies fall with Al content, all three crossing near 27–29% Al at ~60–80 mJ/m² (figure_003).
